observation.visible_scene: A dance studio with a polished wooden floor, a large wall mirror on the left/center, beige curtains, a frosted whiteboard panel and a wall clock on the right, and bags resting on the floor near the right edge. A man in a black sleeveless 'ZUMBA' shirt, black pants and multicolored sneakers stands with his back to the camera, facing the mirror. The mirror shows his front-facing reflection (chest logo visible) performing the same motions, plus a child in a yellow top standing fairly still behind him and a few background figures reflected on the left. The camera framing of the room (mirror seam, whiteboard, clock, bags) stays fixed across all frames.
visible_changes: The man's arms cycle through a repeating dance pattern: lowered at his sides, then extended out to one side with the opposite elbow bent near the head, then both arms raised overhead in a wide 'V', then lowered again; this alternates left and right over the excerpt.

His torso sways and rotates slightly and his weight shifts between legs, with feet stepping and heels lifting (e.g., left foot raised early, then right foot lifting later), indicating a stepping/hip-swaying rhythm.
The front-facing reflection in the mirror moves in sync with the man's arm and body changes (arms spreading, rising overhead, and tucking).

The child in the reflection remains largely stationary with hands near the chest/face throughout; background reflected figures shift only marginally (a person in teal becomes visible on the left in later frames).
Static elements (room layout, clock, whiteboard, floor bags) do not move, confirming the motion is the dancer's, not the camera's.
outside_clip_unknowns: The music or cue driving the routine, the choreography before t=0 and after the last frame, and whether the arm cycle continues or transitions to a different move.
The full bodies/positions of the reflected child and background people in real space (they are seen only via the mirror).
uncertain_details: Exact footwork/jump pattern and hip rotation magnitude are hard to resolve frame-by-frame.
The precise time on the wall clock is not clearly legible.
Whether the man's gaze/upper-body twist is part of a turn or just sway cannot be confirmed from the rear view.
